speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance. To help me identify the cause, can you tell me if this dizziness feels like the room is spinning, or if it is more of a feeling of unsteadiness?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The patient's report of a constant spinning sensation, rather than the brief episodes typical of BPPV, along with his age and lack of other focal neurologic deficits, points more strongly toward viral labyrinthitis or early Meniere's disease. REQUEST TEST: Audiometry, Vestibular_Swab, Blood_Culture.
